extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, and patent practitioners (and USPTO staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for preparing, submitting, and recording assignments and related documents with the USPTO, and for establishing assignee ownership/authority to take action in patent applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment must be in writing (35 U.S.C. 261)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for patent, patents, or any interest therein, shall be assignable in law by an instrument in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certificate of acknowledgment (properly executed/apostilled where applicable) is prima facie evidence of execution. Case law (e.g., Realvirt, LLC v. Lee) treats assignments as requiring written transfer of the bundle of rights. Ensure the assignment instrument conveys the entire right, title and interest (or clearly specifies fractional interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation to protect against subsequent purchasers/mortgagees
rubrics_metrics.description: An interest that constitutes an assignment, grant, or conveyance shall be void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for valuable consideration, without notice, unless it is recorded in the Patent and Trademark Office within three months from its date or prior to the date of such subsequent purchase or mortgage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely recordation (within three months of execution or before the later purchaser/mortgagee) is necessary to preserve priority versus bona fide purchasers/mortgagees. Recordation is a public-notice mechanism; do not rely solely on private proof of assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use USPTO definitions (37 CFR 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of these regulations: 'Application' means national/international patent applications designating the U.S.; 'Assignment' means a transfer by a party of all or part of its right, title and interest; 'Document' means a document requested to be recorded under §3.11; 'Recorded document' means a document recorded pursuant to §3.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft and classify submission materials consistent with these definitions so the Office correctly treats the submission (e.g., as an assignment vs. other document affecting title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Which documents will be recorded (37 CFR 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of applications, patents, and registrations, and other documents relating to interests in patent applications and patents (with completed cover sheets) will be recorded; other documents affecting title may be recorded as provided or at Director's discretion. Joint research agreements (or excerpts) will be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an appropriate cover sheet referencing the patents/applications. Governmental instruments required by Exec. Order 9424 must be forwarded and recorded as provided. Consult 37 CFR Part 3 for scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment document must be a copy; originals not accepted for return (37 CFR 3.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accept and record only a copy of an original assignment or other document; the Office will not return recorded documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electronic submissions: submit digitized images (TIFF or Director-prescribed) that are legible when printed on 8.5x11 or A4 with 1-inch (2.5 cm) margins. For paper/fax: one side only, 8.5x11 or A4, 1-inch margins, flexible strong white paper. Do not submit originals; if copy is illegible the recorded copy will be illegible.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation required for non-English documents (37 CFR 3.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-English assignment documents will not be recorded unless accompanied by an English translation signed by the translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a signed translator's statement. Absent a proper translation the Office will not record the instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of patent or application required (37 CFR 3.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment relating to a patent must identify the patent by patent number; an assignment relating to a national patent application must identify it by application number; international applications/designs must be identified by their international numbers. If executed before filing the assignment must identify the application by the name(s) of inventor(s) and title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application/patent numbers are not yet known, wording that permits later insertion of the number is acceptable (example language provided). Ensure the identity of the intended application/patent is unambiguous to avoid mis-recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign assignee may designate a domestic representative (35 U.S.C. 293; 37 CFR 3.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee not domiciled in the United States may designate a person residing in the U.S. on whom process or notice of proceedings affecting the patent may be served; the designation should be submitted as a paper separate from any assignment and be clearly labeled 'Designation of Domestic Representative' and signed per 37 CFR 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the domestic representative designation separately (not embedded in the assignment). Provide name and U.S. address for service. Ensure proper signature formalities are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee address must be provided in assignment and cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The address of the assignee may be recited in the assignment document and must be given in the required cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete mailing address for the assignee on both the assignment copy and cover sheet to facilitate correspondence and record accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fees per identified patent/application; check current fee schedule (37 CFR 3.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee is required for each application, patent and registration against which the document is recorded as identified in the cover sheet; some exceptions apply (e.g., governmental documents not affecting title if faxed/electronically submitted or mailed in compliance with §3.27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted electronically the current fee may be set to $0 (per 1.21(h)(1)); paper/fax submissions may incur the fee in 1.21(h)(2). Always check the current USPTO fee schedule before submission. Ensure the cover sheet totals the number of items and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment must be accompanied by a cover sheet with required contents (37 CFR 3.28 and 3.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every document submitted for recording must include a single cover sheet referring to the patent(s)/application(s) or trademark(s)/registration(s) against which the document is to be recorded; the cover sheet must include the name of party conveying the interest, name/address of party receiving the interest, description of interest, identification of interests (patent/app numbers or indication filed together), correspondence address, execution date, and signature. Special items required for joint research agreements and trademark cover sheets are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use one cover sheet for both patents and trademarks; submit separate patent and trademark cover sheets. If cover sheet is incomplete the submission will be returned per §3.51. Include number of items and total fee. For patent applications filed on/after 9/16/2012, if assignment is intended to serve as the oath/declaration, the cover sheet must conspicuously indicate that intent. Form PTO-1595 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic cover sheet signature format (37 CFR 3.31(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an assignment document or name change filed electronically, the person who signs the cover sheet must either place a symbol comprised of letters, numbers, and/or punctuation marks between forward slashes (e.g., /Thomas O’Malley III/) or sign using some other form of electronic signature specified by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting electronically, adopt the /Name/ convention or another USPTO-accepted e-signature method to avoid signature rejection. Ensure the e-sign is placed in the signature block on the electronic submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment records open to public inspection with confidentiality exceptions (37 CFR 1.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment records, digests, and indexes for patents and published patent applications are open to public inspection and images since June 1998 are on the USPTO website; assignment records for unpublished pending applications are not public unless written authority is provided from inventor/applicant/assignee or on petition. Records before May 1, 1957 are maintained by NARA and are open to inspection through NARA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain confidential assignment records for pending/unpublished applications you must provide written authority (from inventor/applicant/assignee/patent practitioner) or submit a petition with fee. When ordering a copy, identify the reel and frame to avoid additional search charges; if unspecified, extra search charges will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not partially open a document; multi-subject documents become public if any covered subject is public
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recorded document contains two or more items, any one of which would be open to public inspection if alone, then the entire document will be open. Thus documents covering trademarks and patents or multiple patent applications become public ab initio once any one application is published or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid combining confidential pending applications with public matters in one document if confidentiality is desired; submit separate documents/cover sheets to preserve confidentiality where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation is ministerial and does not determine validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordation of an assignment is a ministerial act by the USPTO; it is not an Office determination of the validity of the assignment document or its effect on ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret recording as adjudication of title; legal disputes over ownership may require court or other proceedings. Recording gives public notice but does not confer legal validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation in assignment records alone does not permit assignee to take action in application/patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordation of an assignment in the assignment records of the Office does not, by itself, permit the assignee to take action in the application, patent, or other patent proceeding; the assignee must be made of record in the application file (see 37 CFR 1.46 and 3.81(a) and MPEP §325).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To permit an assignee to act in prosecution: (a) make the assignee of record in the application file (e.g., request change of applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2)), and (b) for applications filed on/after 9/16/2012 comply with 37 CFR 3.73(c) (statement establishing ownership). Recordation in assignment records is necessary for public notice but additional steps are needed for procedural authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment may include assignment-statement to serve as oath/declaration (for certain post-AIA applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), 363, or 385 on or after September 16, 2012, an assignment may contain the statements required in an oath or declaration ('assignment-statement'), and if the assignment is made of record in the assignment records, it may be utilized as the oath or declaration (see 35 U.S.C. 115(e), 37 CFR 1.63(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intending to use the assignment as the oath/declaration, include a conspicuous indication on the cover sheet and ensure the assignment contains the required assignment-statement language per 1.63 and MPEP §602.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee must establish ownership to take action (37 CFR 3.73(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee who is not the original applicant first seeks to take action in a matter before the Office for an application filed on or after September 16, 2012, the assignee must establish its ownership to the satisfaction of the Director by filing a 37 CFR 3.73(c) statement in the file: (A) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee and a statement that such evidence was or is being submitted for recordation; or (B) a statement specifying, by reel and frame number, where such evidence is recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3.73(c) statement must be filed prior to or with the paper that requests or takes the action; otherwise the action will not be given effect (the date of a belated 3.73(c) submission becomes the date of the request/action). Documentary evidence must be recorded or concurrently submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign 37 CFR 3.73(c) ownership submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 3.73(c) submission must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. Acceptable signers include: (A) an officer (presumed authority) or person with apparent authority; (B) any person if the submission states that the signer is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; (C) a patent practitioner of record; or (D) a person empowered by an organizational resolution (copy of resolution submitted or previously on file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the signer lacks clear officer title or stated authority, include evidence of authority (e.g., corporate resolution, power of attorney). A power of attorney to a practitioner does not by itself make the practitioner an official organizational officer; include appropriate appointment if practitioner will sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple (partial) assignees must account for the entire interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one assignee (partial assignees) or a combination of partial assignees and inventors hold the right, title and interest, each owner must submit a 3.73(c) statement that either: (A) specifies (by percentage) the extent of its ownership interest so the entirety of the interest is accounted for, or (B) identifies the parties (including inventors) who together own the entire right, title and interest and states that all identified parties own the entire interest (37 CFR 3.73(c)(2)(i)-(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ownership percentages or the parties composing the whole interest are not specified, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as an establishment of ownership interest. Ensure consistency among multiple submissions to avoid refusal or conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting 3.73(c) statements resolved by Director; consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more purported assignees file conflicting 3.73(c) statements in an application or proceeding, the Director will determine which purported assignee, if any, will be permitted to take action. If the ownership deemed controlling is contested by another party on the record, the matter will be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for resolving procedural issues (37 CFR 3.73(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you face conflicting recorded statements, be prepared for Director-level resolution and consider filing your own application if appropriate. Keep chain-of-title documentation clear to avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations when ownership must and need not be established (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership must be established to take certain actions (e.g., sign a request for status, appoint own registered attorney to prosecute, sign a disclaimer, consent to reissue, sign a Fee Transmittal). Ownership need not be established for other actions (e.g., sign a small entity statement, certain property-rights statements, affidavits where inventor is unavailable, certificates under 37 CFR 1.8, reexamination requests under 1.510).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before acting in a matter, verify whether the intended action requires a 3.73(c) statement; consult the MPEP examples. For juristic entities acting on/after 9/16/2012, representation by a patent practitioner may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental and Secret Registers for governmental interests (37 CFR 3.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will maintain a Departmental Register to record governmental interests required by Executive Order 9424 (not open to public inspection except as provided) and may maintain a Secret Register at the submitting department's request; instruments may be kept secret and examined only with written authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government agencies submitting instruments requesting secrecy must provide written authority; when secrecy is lifted the instrument must be recorded again in the Departmental Register. The Departmental Register instruments will be made available to the public as provided in §1.12.
